# My plan for this year

Let me think this through. I've only been at this four years, so I still lean on what the extension guy says and what the older farmers in the village do. But 200 mu is a lot of land — I can't farm it like my neighbor with his 15 mu. I have to hire labor and run machines. My wife and I work full time on the farm; our two kids are in school and only help on weekends and during harvest rush.

## How I'm dividing up the land

- **Wheat–maize rotation: 160 mu.** This is the backbone. Everyone around here does it, the machinery is set up for it, and I know what to expect. I'm not going to mess with what works on most of my land.
- **Cabbage: 20 mu.** Good money if I time the market right, but it eats labor like crazy. I'll plant it on my field closest to the road so the truck can get in for harvest.
- **Stevia: 20 mu.** I signed a contract with the buying station again this year. Price is fixed, which I like — takes some of the gambling out of it. My neighbor Lao Wang has been doing stevia six years and he walks me through the tricky parts.

## Wheat (160 mu)

I plant around October 10th, give or take a few days depending on when the maize comes off. I use an improved variety — Jimai 22 has worked well for me and for the farmers I talk to. Extension says 15 kg N per mu is optimal but honestly I do about 18. I'd rather spend a little extra on urea than watch my wheat turn yellow at jointing. I put down compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base at planting, maybe 40 kg/mu, then topdress urea at jointing in March. If the crop looks weak I'll do a second topdress at booting. I irrigate 3 times normally — pre-winter, jointing, and filling. If March is dry I might add one. Pumping from the well costs money so I don't overdo it. Target yield: around 480 kg/mu. Last year I got 470 so I think that's reasonable.

## Maize (160 mu)

Tight turnaround after wheat harvest. I hire a custom no-till planter — I don't have time or equipment to plow 160 mu in a week. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or similar. Around 17 kg N/mu, usually as one base application of compound plus a topdress at big trumpet stage. Summer rains usually cover the water so I might only irrigate once or twice if July is dry. Pests — I watch for armyworm and corn borer, spray if I see damage. Target: 520 kg/mu.

## Cabbage (20 mu)

This is where most of my labor cost goes. Transplant in August for autumn harvest. Heavy feeder — I put down plenty of base compound plus manure I buy from a pig farm nearby, then side-dress urea twice during heading. Irrigate often, probably 5–6 times through the season. I hire women from the village for transplanting and harvest — 4–5 of them for several weeks. Risky crop because the price swings a lot, but if the market is decent I make more per mu on cabbage than on anything else.

## Stevia (20 mu)

Planted in April, harvested in autumn. The contract buyer gives me technical guidance so I basically follow their fertilizer program — lighter on N than cabbage, around 12 kg N/mu. One or two cuttings depending on growth. Irrigation 2–3 times. Less stress on this crop because the price is set.

## The tight spots

Money: my biggest upfront cost is in autumn (wheat planting + cabbage) and late spring (maize inputs + stevia). I keep enough cash back for emergencies — don't want to get caught short if the well pump breaks or a sprayer needs repair. Labor: I have hired help lined up for harvest peaks. The cabbage labor is what worries me most — if I can't find enough women to cut cabbage when it's ready I lose quality fast.
